---
title: "10. Noise analysis"
subtitle: "Visualize density, integrated RMS, and the component budget"
julia:
  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../../AmberMakie/docs"]
---

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(@__DIR__, "../../../AmberMakie/docs"))
using Amber, AmberMakie, CairoMakie
CairoMakie.activate!()
set_theme!(theme_amber_light())
```

Noise density answers what happens in a narrow band; integrated noise answers
what the whole measurement band contributes. AmberMakie keeps those views tied
to the same `NoiseResult`.

```{julia}
@circuit MakieNoisyDivider() begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    output = node()
    Source = voltage_source(input, gnd; dc=1V, ac=1V)
    Rsource = resistor(input, output; value=10kΩ)
    Rload = resistor(output, gnd; value=10kΩ)
    Cload = capacitor(output, gnd; value=10nF)
end

noise_result = noise(MakieNoisyDivider(), 10Hz => 1MHz;
    output=voltage(:output), input=:Source, points=241);
```

```{julia}
figure = Figure(size=(1150, 560))
noiseplot(figure[1, 1], noise_result; referred=:output, color="#0072B2")
integratednoiseplot(figure[1, 2], noise_result;
    referred=:output, color="#D55E00")
Label(figure[0, :], "Output noise density and cumulative RMS"; fontsize=20)
figure
```

## Find the dominant components

The budget plot groups source mechanisms by component. This is much more useful
for design iteration than a single total-noise curve.

```{julia}
budget_figure = Figure(size=(900, 520))
noisebudgetplot(budget_figure[1, 1], noise_result; group=:component)
Label(budget_figure[0, 1], "Frequency-dependent output-noise budget"; fontsize=20)
budget_figure
```

The adapter exposes the same contribution data to Julia. We can print the
available contributor labels before deciding how to group or filter them.

```{julia}
contributions = noisecontributionview(noise_result; group=:component)
(
    contributors=contributions.labels,
    frequency_points=length(noise_result.frequencies),
    output=string(noise_result.output),
)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
For interactive band selection, use `handle = workbench(noise_result)` and
`setinterval!(handle.cursors, 100Hz => 100kHz)`. The workbench updates its RMS
measurement and contribution ranking together.
:::
